About

I enjoy turning curious questions into systems I can design, build, and test.

My interest in Electrical Engineering began with a simple question: why does this work? I follow it from the circuit on the board to the code that drives it, and I am most engaged where hardware and software meet, in embedded systems, IoT, and robotics.

I am early in my engineering journey and treat that as an advantage. I look for unfamiliar problems, learn through iteration, and value working with people who like to build.

Beyond engineering, I pursue two creative interests that sharpen my attention to detail and discipline.

  • MusicI play piano and guitar at an advanced level, a personal passion I practise for the enjoyment of it.PianoGuitar
  • Video editingI am proficient in professional and mobile editing software, and use it to turn projects and ideas into clear visual stories.DaVinci ResolveAdobe Premiere ProFilmoraCapCut

Projects

Coursework & experiments

Electrical Engineering Mini Projects

Small experiments exploring how circuits sense the world around them. One of them is simulated online, so you can open it and see the circuit run.

  • Light sensing (LDR)
  • Temperature sensing
  • Humidity detection
  • Wokwi simulation
View project on Wokwi ↗
Economic Survival Project

Smart Room System

A low-cost IoT room that senses light, temperature, humidity and smoke, then switches the lamp, fan, AC and alarm on its own. Built around economic survival: on a tight budget, electricity should only be spent when the room needs it, and the room should stay safe without anyone watching.

Hardware: ESP32 (WiFi) · LDR · DHT22 · MQ-2 · ESP-CAM

  • LDR < 40% lightLamp on automatically, off when bright
  • DHT22 ≥ 28 °CDesk fan on
  • DHT22 ≥ 30 °CAC on
  • DHT22 ≥ 75% humidityFlagged as high
  • MQ-2 smokeAlarm + WiFi notification
  • ESP-CAMDoor camera streams over WiFi

Move the sensor sliders to see the lamp, fan, AC and alarm react. Drag to rotate, +/− to zoom.
